notes: S330 full nine-axis website audit. Every emitted item names a conversion or information-finding outcome. Premises were re-verified against the post-sync tree; two S329 sub-premises were disproven and omitted. The plan preserves D-S329.7 analysis-before-merge, D-S329.8 final-tree receipt ordering, SOUL identity/membership/security constraints, staging-before-production, and direct-to-main release authorization.

items.title: One intelligence spine — fold Nervous System into Studio Pulse and make discovery structural
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: /nervous-system/ and /studio-pulse/ remain separate public destinations, both remain in the canonical header/footer manifest, and only 3 HTML pages carry the .intel-suite navigation despite an 11-page intelligence cluster. The sitemap is still generated in a workflow shell block with path-substring exclusions, which is why legitimate vault-member routes disappeared and robots-noindex pages stayed discoverable. Outcome: humans and agents reach one coherent live-intelligence home, every intelligence page exposes the same wayfinding, and the sitemap reflects semantic indexability instead of brittle path text.
items.recipe: Create a shared intelligence-suite renderer/contract, migrate Studio Pulse to absorb the Nervous System signal digest, replace /nervous-system/ with a permanent redirect stub and redirect rule, update header/footer/agents/entity graph/evidence graph consumers, add /status/ and /search/ to Resources, replace workflow sitemap shell logic with a git-tracked structural generator that parses robots directives, and lock route/nav/sitemap behavior with both-direction tests plus rendered-pixel QA.

L1.recipe: Redirect /nervous-system/, update manifest/navigation, and fix the two known sitemap omissions.

L2.recipe: L1 plus shared 11-route intelligence navigation, semantic robots-noindex sitemap generation, source/consumer contract tests, and every-theme desktop/mobile visual review.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a machine-readable intelligence-route registry consumed by nav, entity graph, agents.json, sitemap, evidence graph, and page generators so future route drift becomes structurally impossible.

items.title: Route consolidation with proof — turn duplicate funnels and orphan islands into two clear journeys
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: membership, membership-value, vaultsparked, vault-portal, join, vault-wall, community, notebook, ip, share, brand/system, ignis/roi, security/trusted-types, legacy franchise-architect, and solara roots all still exist as independent routes; the canonical nav still advertises the redundant membership destinations. D-S329.7 requires written per-cluster analysis before any merge. Outcome: visitors choose a tier or enter the member experience without parallel explanations, and every retired route preserves its unique value through a deliberate destination or explicit retirement.
items.recipe: Generate and append a per-cluster merge analysis from live inbound-link, unique-section, generator-owner, canonical, and robots evidence; then consolidate membership 5→2, leaderboard surfaces to one home, link-or-retire the orphan batch, expand /projects/ from the registry instead of a hand-maintained partial catalog, add permanent redirects/canonical/noindex policy, and verify all inbound paths, structured data, and mobile/theme states.

L1.recipe: Write evidence-backed merge analyses and retire only exact duplicates with redirects.

L2.recipe: L1 plus full membership 5→2, leaderboard consolidation, orphan batch disposition, registry-derived project catalog, redirect/canonical tests, and rendered QA.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a reusable route-consolidation court that inventories inbound links, unique semantic blocks, generator ownership, canonical targets, and redirect-chain depth before future merges.

items.title: Complete the public trust path — prove security controls, challenge abuse, and open Ask Founders
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: api/security-posture.json reports only 6/8 controls because build-security-posture searches the package script text for csp-audit.mjs and verify-supply-chain.mjs while the canonical build runner has moved to a composed step registry. Contact and Desk dispatch have no Turnstile siteverify flow even though credentials and the shared client helper are ready. The Worker already rate-limits /ask-founders/submit but no public /ask-founders/ page exists. Outcome: visitors see a truthful clean posture, abusive submissions fail at the edge before provider work, and a bounded founder-question surface actually reaches its provisioned route.
items.recipe: Resolve control evidence from the canonical build-step registry rather than package-string coincidence; implement edge-first Turnstile verification for contact and Dispatch in one release unit, mount the existing helper with accessible failure/retry states, build /ask-founders/ against its bounded Worker route, add tokenless/invalid/valid-path unit and browser tests, and visually inspect every touched state across themes and viewports.

L1.recipe: Fix security-posture evidence resolution and build the Ask Founders page against the existing rate-limited route.

L2.recipe: L1 plus edge-first Turnstile on contact and Dispatch, strict rejection tests, accessible retry UX, exact CSP coverage, and staged rendered verification.

L3.recipe: L2 plus privacy-safe abuse receipts and a reusable challenged-form contract shared by future Studio public forms.

items.title: Move scheduled prose to the free inference plane and stop rebuilding the world for feed refreshes
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: generate-vault-narrative.mjs still calls Anthropic daily at maxTokens 220 and the workflow injects the Anthropic key; the repo already has a tested free Hetzner desk-inference.chat() client with thinking:false support. refresh-live-data.yml still runs the full npm build before a long hand-maintained tail. update-journal-dates.mjs is not in the build chain, and no monthly draft-for-review journal revival exists. Outcome: scheduled editorial automation has zero variable model cost, enough output budget for grounded prose, and feed refreshes do only the dependency closure they own.
items.recipe: Migrate vault narrative to desk-inference.chat() with maxTokens >=512, thinking:false, source-grounding post-checks, honest preservation on unavailable inference, and workflow capability swap; introduce a named slim runDerivedBuilds profile with coverage assertions for refresh-live-data; add a monthly journal-revival draft lane using the same advisory inference path, never auto-publish, and wire deterministic journal-date normalization into the canonical build.

L1.recipe: Move vault narrative to free inference with grounding checks and remove the paid secret from its workflow.

L2.recipe: L1 plus slim derived-build profile, coverage court, monthly draft-only journal revival, deterministic date normalization, and end-to-end workflow self-tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus shared grounded-editorial contracts, token/latency receipts, replay fixtures, and an abstention-first editorial review queue.

items.title: Make the sitewide shell safe to regenerate
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: scripts/propagate-nav.mjs still owns hand-maintained NAV_GAMES and NAV_PROJECTS arrays, hand-built intelligence/resource links, and shell asset references; S329 demonstrated that a bare run clobbers 126 pages. The site already has game-registry, public-intelligence catalog, footer-manifest, and hashed shell manifests that can serve as authorities. Outcome: a navigation refresh cannot demote live projects, drop resource links, or replace hashed assets with stale names.
items.recipe: Derive game/project status groups, intelligence/resources links, footer counts, and shell asset filenames from existing registries/manifests; add --check/--dry-run contract tests that compare rendered navigation against the live catalog and fail before writes; then run the propagator only after parity is proven.

L1.recipe: Add a no-write parity gate that fails on every currently stale hand-maintained array/reference.

L2.recipe: L1 plus replace all hand arrays with registry/manifest reads and prove dry-run produces no unexpected page diff.

L3.recipe: L2 plus extract a reusable canonical shell renderer consumed directly by page generators so propagation becomes a compatibility migration rather than the long-term owner.

items.title: Make proof ordering executable — stale visual/mobile receipts must fail on the final built tree
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: D-S329.8 records that build re-stamps pages after mobile and visual receipts bind their hashes; current discipline relies on humans running build → mobile → build:check in the right order. Existing receipts carry source hashes, but no meta-gate compares them to the current tree. Outcome: release evidence cannot claim a page state that a later generator already changed.
items.recipe: Build check-receipt-ordering.mjs to derive current hashes for every receipt-bound route/artifact, compare mobile-runtime and docs/visual-qa/LATEST.json provenance to the final tree, fail with exact stale paths, add mutation self-tests for build-after-receipt and unrelated changes, wire it after all generators in build:check and before deployment.

L1.recipe: Compare the two current receipt source hashes to the current built tree and fail on mismatch.

L2.recipe: L1 plus per-route diagnostics, mutation self-tests, build-chain reachability, and release-candidate manifest binding.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a generic proof-dependency DAG that timestamps/hashes every rendered, mobile, Lighthouse, and staging receipt against one candidate generation.

items.title: Spend measured headroom — reduce the 187 KB stylesheet and raise performance floors only to proven capacity
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: the main stylesheet remains roughly 187 KB, visual QA retains hundreds of PNGs without a declared lifecycle, and the Franchise Architect surface has a recorded pointerenter INP hotspot. The Lighthouse floor is still calibrated below recent measured green runs. Outcome: repeat visits move less CSS, interaction latency improves on the known hotspot, and the release gate ratchets to observed capacity without fabricating a target.
items.recipe: Inventory selector usage and JS-resident asset references before pruning; split or deduplicate shared CSS with byte and unused-rule measurements, fix the Franchise Architect pointerenter path using measured event work, implement a hash/receipt-aware visual PNG retention policy, benchmark staging at mobile and desktop, and raise the Lighthouse floor only to the lower confidence bound of repeated measurements.

L1.recipe: Fix the known pointerenter hotspot and remove only proven-dead shell assets/selectors.

L2.recipe: L1 plus measured CSS reduction, visual receipt retention tooling, repeated Lighthouse samples, and an evidence-backed floor ratchet.

L3.recipe: L2 plus route-tier critical CSS budgets, interaction tracing receipts, and an automatic conservative floor proposal derived from rolling successful runs.

items.title: Close the human↔studio↔agent loop — real Eternal Intelligence, member feedback, and capability actions
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: Eternal Intelligence remains a placeholder without a model call; the portal has no member-to-studio feedback panel despite page_feedback already being the canonical anonymous feedback table; and agents.json advertises discovery but no authenticated action API backed by Obelisk agent grants. Outcome: members can ask the studio intelligence layer real bounded questions, send actionable feedback, and agents can perform explicit capability-scoped actions with receipts rather than scrape pages.
items.recipe: Reuse ask-ignis token metering/cache/persona for a real Eternal Intelligence function, deploy the function before portal UI; add a member feedback panel reusing page_feedback contracts; define a minimal agent action API with Obelisk short-lived agent grants, deny-by-default scopes, idempotency, and signed human/agent receipts; update agents.json/llms/JSON-LD and verify auth/session/logout boundaries without introducing project-local identity.

L1.recipe: Ship the real Eternal Intelligence call and a feedback panel using existing contracts.

L2.recipe: L1 plus capability-scoped agent actions, Obelisk grants, idempotency, signed receipts, discovery metadata, and staged end-to-end tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a user-visible action ledger, revocation/status UI, bounded multi-step agent workflows, and policy fuzz tests.

items.title: Give generated evidence and Desk art durable memory
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: the evidence graph models one .cache artifact while 17 other byte-checked cache consumers remain undeclared; Desk publication has session-level visual proof but no per-story receipt or recent-art diversity memory. Outcome: derived cache strands fail before publish, every story proves its own safe-zone/derivative/render lineage, and repeated visual shorthand is rejected even when bytes differ.
items.recipe: Classify every byte-checked .cache artifact as a graph node or source-local explicit exemption; extend the Desk edition contract with source/derivative hashes, safe-zone geometry, desktop/mobile render hashes, and review state; maintain a bounded diversity ledger over scene archetype, palette, focal arrangement, and satire target; fail promotion on incomplete lineage or excessive repetition and add mutation tests.

L1.recipe: Model/exempt all 17 cache artifacts and emit per-story source/derivative/safe-zone hashes.

L2.recipe: L1 plus desktop/mobile render bindings, bounded diversity memory, publisher rejection logic, and mutation tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus perceptual similarity features, reviewer override receipts, and an edition-level visual contact sheet generated from the contract.

items.title: Repair SIL category integrity — metadata must never be counted as an eleventh score
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: context/PROJECT_STATUS.json stores updatedSession inside silCategoriesV3. The live canon-conformance checker therefore sees 11 categories and sums 1318 against silScore 989; check-status-projection-coherence likewise reduces every object value. The previous green suite did not surface this schema-level contradiction. Outcome: the Hub, closeout board, Canon checker, and status projection agree on exactly ten 0–100 categories whose sum equals silScore.
items.recipe: Move updatedSession to a dedicated metadata field, harden every SIL consumer to select the canonical ten category keys and reject unknown numeric members, update schema/writer/projection/renderer/conformance tests, repair current PROJECT_STATUS without backdating history, and add a regression fixture proving metadata cannot inflate the score.

L1.recipe: Move updatedSession out of silCategoriesV3 and repair current status.

L2.recipe: L1 plus canonical key selection in writer/projection/renderer, schema enforcement, and unknown-key mutation tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a shared SIL receipt parser used by all local score consumers and a cross-surface parity gate.
